assertion_results.text: Impact map or task descriptions explicitly flag at least 3 ambiguities from the feature description
assertion_results.evidence: The impact map 'Excluded requirements' section flags 5 ambiguities: (1) 'Better UI' lacks a frontend repo, (2) 'Search should be faster' has no latency benchmarks or target response times, (3) 'Results should be more relevant' has no ranking criteria or weighting factors, (4) 'Add filters' says 'some kind of filtering capability' without specifying fields, (5) 'Should be fast enough' has no quantified performance target. All 5 are explicitly enumerated in the impact-map.md table at lines 20-23.

assertion_results.text: Plan acknowledges that 'Better UI' (non-MVP) cannot be planned without design mockups or frontend repository and excludes it from scope
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 19: '"Better UI" (non-MVP) | No frontend repository is available in the Repository Registry. The only target repository (trustify-backend) is a Rust backend service. UI improvements require a frontend repository to be added to the project configuration.' It is listed in the 'Excluded requirements' table and no UI task was generated.

assertion_results.text: Tasks still follow the task-description-template.md format despite ambiguous requirements
assertion_results.evidence: All 4 tasks contain the template's required sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Modify (and Files to Create where applicable), Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements, Verification Commands, Dependencies. Optional sections (API Changes in Task 3, Reuse Candidates in Tasks 1-4, Documentation Updates in Task 3) are included where applicable and omitted where not, matching the template rule 'Omit sections that don't apply.'

assertion_results.text: Tasks document assumptions where they fill in missing details, labeled as assumptions pending clarification
assertion_results.evidence: None of the 4 task description files contain the word 'assumption' or the phrase 'pending clarification.' Task 3's description notes 'The feature requirement (TC-9002) calls for "some kind of filtering capability" -- this task implements filtering by the most commonly useful dimensions based on the existing data model' but does not label this as an assumption pending clarification. The impact map mentions 'The planning assumes entity-type, severity, and date-range filters' (line 22) but this is in the impact map, not in the task descriptions, and lacks a 'pending clarification' label. Task 1's description provides rationale for column choices but doesn't mark them as assumptions.

assertion_results.evidence: All 4 tasks have '## Repository\ntrustify-backend' as the first section -- a single repository name with no additional repos listed. Task 1 line 1-2, Task 2 line 1-2, Task 3 line 1-2, Task 4 line 1-2.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:', not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string
assertion_results.evidence: All four digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-4-digest.md) contain the marker '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-adf:<computed-after-refetch>' where '<computed-after-refetch>' is a placeholder string, not a 64-character lowercase hex hash. The files explicitly state 'The digest cannot be pre-computed because Jira normalizes content during storage. The actual digest value depends on the ADF representation returned by the Jira API after creation.' The assertion requires exactly 64 lowercase hex characters after the prefix, not a placeholder.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention references use the prescribed format. Task 1: 'Applies: task creates migration/src/m0002_search_indexes/mod.rs matching the convention's migration file scope' and 'Applies: task modifies migration/src/lib.rs matching the convention's .rs file scope'. Task 2: three convention entries all ending with 'Applies: task modifies modules/search/src/service/mod.rs matching the convention's .rs file scope'. Task 3: four convention entries citing specific files (endpoints/mod.rs, common/src/db/query.rs) matching the convention's .rs file scope. Task 4: two convention entries citing tests/api/search.rs matching the convention's .rs file scope. No inapplicable conventions are listed -- e.g., Task 1 (migration) correctly excludes Endpoint registration, Response types, Query helpers, Testing, and Caching conventions. No 'Not applicable' annotations appear anywhere.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 48: 'Priority: Normal (propagated -- not "Undefined")'. summary-comment.md 'Inherited Field Values' section: 'Priority: Normal (propagated to all tasks and epics -- not "Undefined")'. Jira Operations Log shows all 4 tasks and 2 epics have additional_fields containing '"priority": {"name": "Normal"}'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 49: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.6.0 (propagated -- fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults configured)'. summary-comment.md 'Inherited Field Values': 'Fix Version: RHTPA 1.6.0 (propagated to all tasks and epics -- Feature has fixVersions set and fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults configured)'. Jira Operations Log shows all 4 tasks and 2 epics have '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.6.0"}]' in additional_fields.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Field Values' section (lines 24-26): 'Priority: Normal (propagated to all tasks and epics -- not "Undefined")' and 'Fix Version: RHTPA 1.6.0 (propagated to all tasks and epics -- Feature has fixVersions set and fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults configured)'. The impact-map.md also has a 'Field Inheritance' section (lines 46-49) with the same information.

assertion_results.text: No documentation task is generated because the feature description does not contain a Documentation Considerations section
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md line 69: 'Documentation task: Not generated. The Feature description has no "Documentation Considerations" section.' The 4 generated tasks are: (1) search performance indexes, (2) optimize search queries, (3) add search filters, (4) integration tests. None is a standalone documentation task.

assertion_results.text: No testing tasks are generated because no testing readiness template is present in the eval fixture files
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md line 70: 'Testing tasks: Not generated. No testing readiness template found at docs/testing-readiness.md in the target repository.' The SDLC workflow distinguishes between template-generated testing tasks (from a testing readiness template) and regular feature-decomposition tasks. Task 4 ('Add integration tests for search improvements') is a regular engineering task produced by feature decomposition, not a testing-readiness-template-generated testing task. No testing readiness template file exists in the eval fixture files.
